title: Pure Substances and Mixtures
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Pure Substances and Mixtures Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Use the particle theory to describe pure substances and mixtures; distinguish elements and compounds; classify mixtures as mechanical mixtures, suspensions and solutions. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Pure Substances and Mixtures)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets on the particle theory, pure substances, elements, compounds and kinds of mixtures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A pure substance has one kind of particle.
key_sub: Mixtures have two or more; you can see the parts of a mechanical mixture but not of a solution.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of particles that are always moving and have spaces between them.

  • Pure substances have only one kind of particle: elements (one kind of atom) and compounds (atoms joined).
  • Mixtures have two or more substances: mechanical mixtures, suspensions and solutions.
  • A solution looks like one substance because the solute is dissolved.
Example

Is salt water a pure substance?

it has salt and water

Answer: no, it is a solution

Example

Is water an element or a compound?

H₂O has hydrogen and oxygen

Answer: a compound

Common mistakes

  • Thinking 'pure' means 'clean' or 'natural'.
  • Thinking solutions are pure substances because they look the same.
  • Mixing up elements and compounds.

faq.q: What is the particle theory of matter?
faq.a: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving, have spaces between them and attract each other. Heat makes them move faster.

faq.q: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
faq.a: An element has only one kind of atom. A compound has two or more kinds of atoms joined together.

faq.q: What are the kinds of mixtures?
faq.a: Mechanical mixtures (parts visible), suspensions (cloudy, settle out) and solutions (look like one substance).

items.q: Which word means a mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent?
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q: Is sea water a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: What is a suspension?
c: a cloudy mixture whose particles settle if left standing
items.e: Muddy water and some salad dressings are suspensions.

items.q: Which word means the substance that dissolves?
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q: What does 'soluble' mean?
c: the liquid that the solute dissolves in
a solution in which no more solute can dissolve
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q: Which is a pure substance?
items.e: Distilled water has only water particles.

items.q: Which is a mixture?
items.e: Mixtures contain two or more substances.

items.q: What does 'solution' mean?
c: the solid left in the filter paper
a mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent
the liquid that the solute dissolves in
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q: What does 'solute' mean?
c: the solid left in the filter paper
a solution in which no more solute can dissolve
a mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q:

sample 2melts between −3 °C and −1 °C
sample 3melts between −6 °C and −2 °C
Kai tested three samples that were all sold as water. How can you tell a substance is pure?
c: It melts and boils at fixed, sharp temperatures.
items.e: Pure means only one substance.

items.q:
Sample of 'water'Melting point
sample 2melts between −3 °C and −1 °C
sample 3melts between −6 °C and −2 °C
sample 1melts at exactly 0 °C
Leah tested three samples that were all sold as water. Which sample is the most impure?
items.e: Impurities lower the melting point and make it melt over a range.

items.q: Is pure gold a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: What does 'saturated solution' mean?
c: the liquid that passes through the filter paper
the liquid that the solute dissolves in
a solution in which no more solute can dissolve
items.e: Learn the key words of dissolving and filtering.

items.q: What does the particle theory say about particles of matter?
c: They are the same in every substance.
They are always moving and have spaces between them.
items.e: Particles move faster when heated.

items.q: Is soil a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q:
Sample of 'water'Melting point
sample 3melts between −6 °C and −2 °C
sample 1melts at exactly 0 °C
sample 2melts between −3 °C and −1 °C
Emma tested three samples that were all sold as water. Which sample is pure water?
items.e: A pure substance melts at one sharp temperature.

items.q: What is a mechanical mixture?
c: a mixture that looks like one substance
a mixture where you can see the different parts
items.e: Granola is a mechanical mixture.

items.q: Is milk a pure substance or a mixture?
c: a mixture (it contains water, fats, proteins and sugar)
items.e: Milk is a colloid, a kind of mixture.

items.q: Is orange juice a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: Is table salt (sodium chloride) a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: Is air a compound or a mixture?
c: a compound, because it has oxygen
a mixture, because its gases are not chemically combined
items.e: The amounts of gases in air can vary.

items.q: Which is a compound?
items.e: Compounds have two or more kinds of atoms joined together.

items.q: Which of these elements is a non-metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: What is a compound?
c: two elements mixed but not combined
a substance made of two or more elements chemically combined
items.e: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

items.q: Which of these elements is a non-metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: What is an element?
c: a substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical methods
a substance made of two kinds of atoms
items.e: Elements are the basic building blocks of matter.

items.q: Melamine was illegally added to milk to make it seem higher in protein. What does this show?
c: Knowing the chemical composition of food helps to keep it safe.
All chemicals in food are harmful.
items.e: Food testing checks what is really in food.

items.q: Which of these elements is a metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: Is soda water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: Is copper(II) sulfate dissolved in water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: Is chalk powder shaken in water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: Iron and sulfur are heated to form iron(II) sulfide. Which is true of the product?
c: It has different properties from iron and sulfur.
It is still attracted to a magnet like iron.
items.e: A compound has new properties.

items.q: Which of these elements is a metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: Which statement about mixtures is correct?
c: They always have a fixed composition.
The substances are not chemically combined and can be separated by physical methods.
items.e: Air, sea water and soil are mixtures.

items.q: Is muddy water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: Which of these elements is a non-metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: Why is it important to know if a product is a mixture?
c: The parts may be separated and some may be harmful or recyclable.
items.e: Labels list the parts of a mixture.

items.q: Which of these elements is a non-metal?
items.e: In the Periodic Table, metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

items.q: Is flour stirred into water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: What is a pure substance?
c: a mix of two or more substances
a substance made of only one kind of particle
items.e: Pure substances include elements and compounds.

items.q: A 250 g brass key is heated and expands. What happens to its density?
c: It stays the same, because the mass is the same.
It increases, because the mass increases.
It increases, because the particles get bigger.
It decreases, because the same mass takes up a larger volume.
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume. The volume increases while the mass stays the same.

items.q: A 150 g glass marble is heated and expands. What happens to the size of its particles?
items.e: Only the spaces between the particles increase.

items.q: A spray of air freshener can soon be smelt across the classroom. What is the best explanation?
c: The particles were pushed by convection only.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
Diffusion: air freshener particles diffused through the air.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: A 120 g brass key is heated and expands. What is its mass now?
items.e: No particles are added or removed, so the mass does not change.

items.q: Oxygen moves from the air in the lungs into the blood. What is the best explanation?
c: The particles were pushed by convection only.
Diffusion: oxygen moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: A balloon left in the sun gets bigger. Which explains this?
c: The air inside expands as its particles move faster and further apart.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: A 60 g steel rod is heated and expands. What happens to the size of its particles?
items.e: Only the spaces between the particles increase.

items.q: An 80 g steel rod is heated and expands. What happens to its density?
c: It increases, because the mass increases.
It stays the same, because the mass is the same.
It decreases, because the same mass takes up a larger volume.
It increases, because the particles get bigger.
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume. The volume increases while the mass stays the same.

items.q: Power cables sag more on a hot afternoon. Which explains this?
c: The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The cables expand and become longer when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: A tea bag is put into hot water and the colour spreads. What is the best explanation?
c: Diffusion: tea particles diffused into the water.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
The particles were pushed by convection only.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: A 60 g glass marble is heated and expands. What happens to its density?
c: It increases, because the particles get bigger.
It increases, because the mass increases.
It decreases, because the same mass takes up a larger volume.
It stays the same, because the mass is the same.
items.e: Density = mass ÷ volume. The volume increases while the mass stays the same.

items.q: Which state of matter cannot be poured and keeps its shape?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: Which state of matter has particles far apart that move quickly in all directions?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: Which state of matter has particles in a regular pattern that vibrate on the spot?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: Which state of matter has the strongest forces between its particles?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: Bridges have expansion joints with small gaps. Which explains this?
c: The bridge can expand on hot days without buckling.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: Which state of matter flows and takes the shape of its container but keeps a fixed volume?
items.e: Use the particle model: arrangement, movement and forces.

items.q: A 60 g aluminum ring is heated and expands. What is its mass now?
items.e: No particles are added or removed, so the mass does not change.

items.q: The liquid in a thermometer rises when it is warmed. Which explains this?
c: The liquid expands as its particles move further apart.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: Which method separates an insoluble solid from a liquid?
items.e: Sand from water.

items.q: When carbon dioxide dissolves in water to make soda water, what is the solvent?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: What is a pure substance in science?
c: a single element or compound with nothing else mixed in
items.e: Pure orange juice is not pure in science.

items.q: When instant coffee dissolves in hot water to make coffee, what is the solute?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
items.e: Air looks the same throughout.

items.q: Which of these is a mixture but not a solution?
items.e: In sand in water you can still see the separate parts. Nothing is dissolved evenly.

items.q: Which of these is a solution?
items.e: Lemonade made from powder has one substance dissolved evenly in water, so you cannot see the parts. The others are mixtures with parts you can see.

items.q: When copper(II) sulfate dissolves in water to make a blue solution, what is the solvent?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: When oil paint dissolves in turpentine to make thinned paint, what is the solute?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: When salt dissolves in water to make salt solution, what is the solvent?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: Which of these is a mixture but not a solution?
items.e: In a bowl of fruit you can still see the separate parts. Nothing is dissolved evenly.

items.q: Which of these is a solution?
items.e: Sugar water has one substance dissolved evenly in water, so you cannot see the parts. The others are mixtures with parts you can see.

items.q: Which of these is a mixture but not a solution?
items.e: In a salad you can still see the separate parts. Nothing is dissolved evenly.

items.q: What happens to salt when it dissolves in water?
c: It breaks into tiny particles that spread between the water particles.
items.e: It is still there.

items.q: What does distillation use to separate liquids?
items.e: Boil, then condense.

items.q: Which is an element?
items.e: Elements are made of one kind of atom.

items.q: What is a mixture?
c: two or more substances that are not chemically joined
items.e: They can be separated.

items.q: What is a solution?
c: a mixture you can see the parts of
a mixture that looks like one substance because one part is dissolved in another
items.e: Salt water is a solution.

items.q: When sugar dissolves in tea to make sweet tea, what is the solvent?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: When salt dissolves in water to make salt solution, what is the solute?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: 10 g of salt dissolves completely in 80 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 10 + 80 = 90 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.

items.q: Why should a distillation flask never be heated until dry?
c: It could crack or overheat and is unsafe.
items.e: Safety matters in every method.

items.q: 2 g of salt dissolves completely in 250 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 2 + 250 = 252 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.

items.q: Why is the start line kept above the level of the solvent?
c: so the ink does not just dissolve into the solvent in the beaker
so the paper does not tear
items.e: Careful method.

items.q: Why is the start line of a chromatogram drawn in pencil, not ink?
c: Pencil does not dissolve and run up the paper.
items.e: Avoid extra spots.

items.q: 65 g of pebbles is mixed with 233 g of sand. What is the mass of the mixture?
items.e: Nothing is added or lost when you mix: 65 + 233 = 298 g.

items.q: A sample of 'pure' gold melts over a range of temperatures. What does this suggest?
items.e: Sharp melting point means pure.

items.q: Which diagram best represents a liquid?
c: particles far apart and randomly arranged
particles touching each other but arranged randomly
particles in neat rows touching each other
items.e: Liquid particles are close but not in fixed positions.

items.q: Kai evaporates sea water and gets 3.5 g of salt from 100 g. How much salt would 1 kg of sea water give?
items.e: 1 kg is 10 times 100 g.

items.q: 8 g of salt dissolves completely in 100 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 8 + 100 = 108 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.

items.q: A bottle of perfume is opened in a corner. Why does it take time to smell it across the room?
c: Perfume particles collide with air particles and move in random directions.
Particles only move in straight lines.
items.e: Diffusion is not instant.

items.q: Why is distilled water used in car batteries and steam irons?
c: It is pure, with no dissolved solids to leave deposits.
items.e: Uses of pure substances.

items.q: 43 g of sugar is mixed with 76 g of water. What is the mass of the mixture?
items.e: Nothing is added or lost when you mix: 43 + 76 = 119 g.

items.q: 70 g of salt is mixed with 167 g of water. What is the mass of the mixture?
items.e: Nothing is added or lost when you mix: 70 + 167 = 237 g.

items.q: Ava's chromatogram shows a black ink splits into blue, red and yellow. What does this show?
c: The black ink is a mixture of dyes.
items.e: Different dyes travel different distances.

items.q: 66 g of sand is mixed with 153 g of iron filings. What is the mass of the mixture?
items.e: Nothing is added or lost when you mix: 66 + 153 = 219 g.

items.q: A metal ball just fits through a ring. After the ball is heated, it cannot pass through. Why?
c: The particles of the ball got bigger.
The ring shrank when the ball was heated.
The ball expanded because its particles moved further apart.
items.e: Particles do not change size.

items.q: Why does the smell of cooking spread faster in a hot kitchen than in a cold one?
c: Cold air is denser so smells move faster.
Particles move faster at higher temperatures.
items.e: Diffusion is faster when particles have more energy.

items.q: 30 g of salt dissolves completely in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 30 + 200 = 230 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.

items.q: 25 g of sugar dissolves completely in 150 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 25 + 150 = 175 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.
